_about: Scores copied verbatim from the cited tables. Each block names paper, version, page and table, and the exact evaluation set the authors used, which is often NOT the set we run on. tests/test_published.py checks every row against the extracted paper text in data/raw/papers/*.txt.

fintagging_table6.citation: Wang et al., FinTagging: Benchmarking LLMs for Extracting and Structuring Financial Information, arXiv 2505.20650v5
fintagging_table6.eval_set: full FinNI-eval v2 (28,787) and FinCL-eval v2 (261,457); FinCL = rerank of top-200 candidates retrieved with text-embedding-3-small

financebench_table2.citation: Islam et al., FinanceBench: A New Benchmark for Financial Question Answering, arXiv 2311.11944v1
financebench_table2.note: Counts as printed. The GPT-4-Turbo Closed Book row sums to 145, not 150, in the paper itself; kept unchanged.

coling_table4.citation: Wang et al., A Report on Financial Regulations Challenge at COLING 2025, arXiv 2412.11159v2
coling_table4.eval_set: Regulations Challenge test split, organisers' unpublished scorer

xbrl_agent.citation: Han et al., XBRL Agent: Leveraging Large Language Models for Financial Report Analysis, ICAIF 2024
xbrl_agent.note: The paper is not openly available, so no per-model numbers are recorded. The repo README claims tool use improves accuracy by up to 17% (domain queries) and 42% (numeric queries); not used as a published row.
